titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Solomon's Envoy and the Two Lands (ch. 35)
part: ch. 35 — Solomon's Envoy and the Two Lands
about: Solomon sends his envoy Joash son of Jehoiada with gifts to meet the Queen's son on the road. The two sides argue over whose country is better: Joash calls Israel a promised land of milk and honey, and the boy's nobles defend Ethiopia's air, water and harvests, but all agree that Solomon's wisdom surpasses everything. Joash dresses in the garments the boy gives him and goes ahead into Jerusalem. The court is so struck by the boy's likeness to Solomon that they mistake him for the king, and all Israel crowds out to see him.

sentences.t: ፴ወ፭ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘለአከ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ መልአከ ፡ ኀይሉ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ወልዱ ።
sentences.l: 35. Concerning that-which sent king Solomon, messenger-of his-might, to his-son.
sentences.i: Chapter 35: Concerning How King Solomon Sent the Messenger of His Might to His Son
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፴ወ፭ is 35 (spoken ሠላሳ ወኀምስቱ, śälasa wä-ḫaməstu); the ወ inside the numeral is 'and'. በእንተ 'concerning' takes what follows as a construct. ዘለአከ is ዘ- 'that which, how' + ለአከ 'he sent' (3ms perfect): 'concerning that which he sent', the thing sent being the person named next, መልአከ ኀይሉ 'messenger-of his-might' (construct chain: መልአክ 'messenger' + ኀይል 'strength' + -ሁ 'his'). This is Joash's standing title in the chapter: I take 'of his might' as 'his powerful, trusted envoy'. ኀበ ወልዱ 'to his son' (ወልድ + -ሁ).

sentences.t: ወለአከ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ መልአከ ፡ ኀይሉ ፡ ዘያሰምክ ፡ ዲበ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ወመባልዕት ፡ ወመስቴ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይትቀበሎ ፡ ለውእቱ ፡ ነጋዲ ።
sentences.l: And-sent Solomon king, messenger-of his-might, who leans upon his-hand, with gifts and-foods and-drink, that he-might-receive that merchant.
sentences.i: King Solomon sent the messenger of his might, the one who leaned upon his hand (?), with gifts and food and drink, to receive that merchant.
sentences.n: ወለአከ 'and he sent'; the order verb-name-title is regular. መልአከ ኀይሉ: see the heading. ዘያሰምክ ዲበ እዴሁ: ዘ- 'who' + ያሰምክ, 3ms imperfect of an A-stem አሰመከ beside ሰምከ 'lean, rest' (the same stem as ኣሰምክ 'I lean' in ch. 24), here intransitive: 'who leans upon his hand'. The sense is not certain: if 'his' is the king's, the envoy is the confidant who leans on the king's hand (my reading); if the verb is truly causative, it is 'on whose hand he (the king) makes himself lean' (?). እዴሁ 'his hand' (እድ + -ሁ). ምስለ 'with'; አምኃ 'gifts'; መባልዕት 'foods' (plural of መብልዕ), ወመስቴ 'and drink'. ከመ ይትቀበሎ is ከመ + subjunctive of ተቀበለ 'receive, welcome' + -ኦ 'him' ('in order to welcome him'). ለውእቱ ነጋዲ 'that merchant': the boy is called ነጋዲ throughout, as the Queen's trading envoy.

sentences.t: ወሖረ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ ሰረገላት ፡ ወበጽሐ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ ወአምኆ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ዘለአከ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፤
sentences.l: And-went with many chariots, and-reached to-him and-paid-homage-to-him and-gave-him all that-which sent to-him Solomon king, and-said-to-him;
sentences.i: He went with many chariots and came to him, and paid him homage, and gave him all that King Solomon had sent to him, and said to him:
sentences.n: Each ወ- opens a new verb, all in the 3ms perfect: ወሖረ 'and he went', ወበጽሐ 'and he reached' (+ ኀቤሁ 'to him', ኀበ + -ሁ), ወአምኆ 'and he paid homage to him' (አምኀ with -ኦ), ወወሀቦ 'and he gave him' (ወሀበ + -ኦ), ወይቤሎ 'and he said to him' (ይቤ + -ሎ). ሰረገላት is the plural of ሰረገላ 'chariot, wheeled carriage'. ዘለአከ ሎቱ 'that which he sent to him' (ሎቱ = ለ- + -ቱ 'him'). The subject of all these verbs is Joash. The unit ends at a ፤ and the speech follows.

sentences.t: አፍጥን ፡ መጺአ ፡ ኀቤየ ፡ እስመ ፡ ነደደ ፡ ልቡ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ በፍቅረ ፡ ዚአከ ፡ እንዳዒ ፡ ዘያአምር ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ እመ ፡ ወልዱ ፡ አንተ ፡ ወኢእመ ፡ እኁሁ ፡ አንተ ፡ ኢኮንከ ፡ ባዕደ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ራእይከ ፡ ወፍኖትከ ፤
sentences.l: Hasten coming to-me, for burned his-heart, to-the-king, in-love-of yours; perhaps he-knows himself whether his-son you and-not-whether his-brother you; not-you-are other from-him in-all your-appearance and-your-way;
sentences.i: "Hurry to come to me, for the king's heart has burned with love of you. Perhaps he himself knows whether you are his son or, if not, his brother (?); you are no stranger to him in all your appearance and your bearing;
sentences.n: አፍጥን 'hasten!' (imperative of አፈጥነ) with መጺአ 'coming' (verbal noun of መጽአ, accusative): 'hasten to come'. ነደደ ልቡ ለንጉሥ: the possessor is stated twice, the suffix on ልቡ 'his heart' and then ለንጉሥ 'to the king', a common Geʿez way of saying 'the king's heart'. በፍቅረ ዚአከ 'in love of you' (ፍቅር in construct + ዚአከ 'of you'). እንዳዒ is a form I cannot identify; 'perhaps' is guessed from the context; ዘያአምር ለሊሁ 'who/that he himself knows'. እመ ... ወኢእመ 'whether ... and if not' is odd; I give 'whether his son or, if not, his brother' and mark it (?). The thrust is clear: the king will see for himself, and the boy is not 'other' (ባዕደ) than he. ኢኮንከ 'you are not' (ኢ- + ኮንከ, 2ms perfect of ኮነ). እምኔሁ 'from him'. ራእይ 'appearance'; ፍኖት 'way, manner'.

sentences.t: ወይእዘኒ ፡ ተንሥእ ፡ ፍጡነ ፡ እስመ ፡ ይቤለኒ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ አፍጥን ፡ ወአምጽኦ ፡ ኀቤየ ፡ በክብር ፡ ወበዕረፍት ፡ ወበተድላ ፡ በፍሥሓ ፡ ወበሐሤት ።
sentences.l: And-now arise quickly, for said-to-me my-lord king: hasten and-bring-him to-me in-glory and-in-rest and-in-delight, in-joy and-in-gladness.
sentences.i: And now, arise quickly, for my lord the king said to me: 'Hurry, and bring him to me with honor, and rest, and delight, in joy and in gladness.'"
sentences.n: ወይእዘኒ 'and now' (ወ- + ይእዜ + -ኒ). ተንሥእ 'arise!' (imperative); ፍጡነ 'quickly' (accusative, adverb). ይቤለኒ 'he said to me' (ይቤ + ለ- + -ኒ). The king's words are quoted inside Joash's speech: አፍጥን ወአምጽኦ 'hasten and bring him' (imperatives; አምጽአ 'bring', with -ኦ). The last phrase stacks nouns each with በ- 'in, with': በክብር 'in honor', ወበዕረፍት 'and in rest', ወበተድላ 'and in delight', then, with no ወ, a second pair በፍሥሓ 'in joy', ወበሐሤት 'and in gladness'. So the ወ joins the first three, is absent before በፍሥሓ, and returns before the last.

sentences.t: አውሥአውእቱ ፡ ወልድ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ኣአኵቶ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እስመ ፡ ረከብኩ ፡ ሞገሰ ፡ እምእግዚእየ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ እርአይ ፡ ገጾ ፡ አስተፈሥሐኒ ፡ ቃሉ ፤
sentences.l: Answered-that son, and-said-to-him: I-thank-him to-God, God-of Israel, for I-found grace from-my-lord king, without I-see his-face; has-gladdened-me his-word;
sentences.i: The son answered him and said: "I give thanks to God, the God of Israel, for I have found favor with my lord the king, before I have even seen his face; his word has made me glad;
sentences.n: The text prints አውሥአውእቱ as one word: አውሥአ 'he answered' + ውእቱ 'that (one)', run together. ወልድ 'son' is the boy. ኣአኵቶ is the 1cs imperfect of አኰተ 'give thanks, praise' + -ኦ 'him' (the thanks are to God, so ለእግዚኣብሔር follows with the object marker ለ-). Bezold prints the 1cs prefix as ኣ- in the published parts too (ኣአኵቶ in ch. 25-26, ኣአምር in ch. 28, ኣፈቅራ in ch. 24), so this is his regular spelling and not an irregularity. አምላከ እስራኤል 'God-of Israel' (construct). ረከብኩ ሞገሰ 'I found grace' (ሞገስ 'grace, favor'), እም 'from' = 'from the side of'. ዘእንበለ እርአይ ገጾ 'without my seeing his face' (ዘእንበለ + 1cs subjunctive; ገጽ 'face' with accusative -ኦ). አስተፈሥሐኒ 'has gladdened me', ቃሉ 'his word' is its subject.

sentences.t: ወይእዘኒ ፡ እሴፈዎ ፡ ለአምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ከመ ፡ ያርእየኒ ፡ ኪያሁ ፡ ወያግብአኒ ፡ በዳኅን ፡ ኀበ ፡ እምየ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ወብሔርየ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፨
sentences.l: And-now I-wait-for-him for-God-of Israel, that he-may-show-me him and-bring-me-back in-safety to my-mother queen and-my-country Ethiopia.
sentences.i: and now I wait for the God of Israel, that He may show me him, and bring me back in safety to my mother the queen and to my country, Ethiopia."
sentences.n: እሴፈዎ is 1cs imperfect of a verb 'to wait for, hope in' + -ዎ 'him' (Dillmann ሴፈወ); the object God then repeats with ለ-: ለአምላከ እስራኤል. ከመ ያርእየኒ ኪያሁ 'that he may show me him' (አርአየ causative of ርእየ 'see', subjunctive + -ኒ 'me'; ኪያሁ is the accusative pronoun); ወያግብአኒ 'and may he bring me back' (አግብአ). በዳኅን 'in safety'. እምየ 'my mother' (እም + -የ); ንግሥት 'queen'; ብሔርየ 'my country'. The ፨ closes the speech and the section.

sentences.t: አውሥአ ፡ ኢዮአስ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዮዳሔ ፡ መልአከ ፡ ኀይሉ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ለበይነ ፡ ልሕክም ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ዝሰ ፡ ኅዳጥ ፡ ወትረክብ ፡ ዘየዐቢ ፡ እምዝ ፡ ፍሥሓ ፡ ወተድላ ፡ እምኀበ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ንጉሥ ፤
sentences.l: Answered Joash son-of Jehoiada, messenger-of his-might, of-king Solomon, and-said-to-him, to-Bäyna-Ləḥkəm: my-lord, this-indeed (is) little; and-you-will-find what-greater than-this, joy and-delight, from my-lord the-king;
sentences.i: Joash son of Jehoiada, the messenger of King Solomon's might, answered and said to Bäyna-Ləḥkəm: "My lord, this is indeed little; you will find, from my lord the king, what is greater than this: joy and delight;
sentences.n: ኢዮአስ ወልደ ዮዳሔ is Joash son of Jehoiada (the name of the Judean king raised by the priest Jehoiada, here borrowed for Solomon's envoy); ወልደ is construct 'son of'. መልአከ ኀይሉ ለንጉሥ ሰሎሞን: the ለ- here is genitival, 'his might, of King Solomon' (the suffix -ሁ anticipates the owner), so Joash is 'Solomon's envoy' and is not being addressed. The addressee is named after ወይቤሎ: ለበይነ ልሕክም, 'to Bäyna-Ləḥkəm'. This is the boy's own name, Bäyna-Ləḥkəm, as in ch. 31-32, with ለ- 'to' marking the person addressed (as ለንጉሥ marks the addressee elsewhere after ይቤሎ). It cannot be Dillmann's preposition ለበይነ 'on account of': that would leave ልሕክም a dangling word and ወይቤሎ without an addressee, whereas Joash is plainly speaking to the boy, whom he then calls እግዚእየ 'my lord'. The etymology of the name stays unresolved, as in ch. 31-32. ዝሰ 'this indeed' (ዝ + emphatic -ሰ); ኅዳጥ 'little'. ወትረክብ 'and you will find' (2ms imperfect); ዘየዐቢ 'what is greater' (ዘ- + 3ms imperfect of ዐበየ). እምዝ 'than this'. ፍሥሓ ወተድላ 'joy and delight', in apposition to ዘየዐቢ. እምኀበ 'from the side of'.

sentences.t: ወበእንተሰ ፡ ዘትብል ፡ እምየ ፡ ወብሔርየ ፡ እምነ ፡ እምከ ፡ ይኄይስ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወእምነ ፡ ሀገርከ ፡ ትኄይስ ፡ ሀገርነ ፡ ዛቲ ፤
sentences.l: and-concerning-indeed what-you-say my-mother and-my-country: than your-mother is-better Solomon king, and-than your-country is-better our-country this;
sentences.i: as for what you say, 'my mother and my country': King Solomon is better than your mother, and this country of ours is better than your country;
sentences.n: ወበእንተሰ 'and as for' (ወ- + በእንተ + emphatic -ሰ). ዘትብል 'what you say' (ዘ- + 2ms imperfect of ብህለ). እምነ እምከ is two words: እምነ 'than, from' before a noun, and እምከ 'your mother' (እም + -ከ); the same እምነ opens ወእምነ ሀገርከ 'and than your country'. ይኄይስ / ትኄይስ 'is better' (ኀየሰ, 3ms / 3fs imperfect; the feminine because ሀገር 'country' is feminine). ሀገርነ ዛቲ 'this our country' (ዛቲ feminine demonstrative placed after).

sentences.t: ወሀገርከሰ ፡ ሰማዕነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ምድረ ፡ በረድ ፡ ወጊሜ ፡ ከመ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ጸዳል ፡ ወመርቄ ፡ ከመ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ደደክ ፡ ወአስሐትያ ፤
sentences.l: And-your-country-indeed we-heard like land-of hail and-mist, like land-of ጸዳል and-መርቄ, like land-of ደደክ and-አስሐትያ;
sentences.i: As for your country, we have heard that it is like a land of hail and mist, like a land of ጸዳል (?) and መርቄ (?), like a land of ደደክ (?) and አስሐትያ (?);
sentences.n: A hard unit; I translate what I can and leave the rest in Geʿez. ወሀገርከሰ 'and as for your country' (-ሰ emphatic, -ከ 'your'); ሰማዕነ 'we heard'. ከመ ምድረ 'like a land of' (ምድር in construct). በረድ 'hail'; ጊሜ 'gloom, mist' (with ወ-). ጸዳል is usually 'brightness' or 'dew', which does not fit a bad-land list; it may be a word for frost or even a place-name (?). መርቄ I cannot place (it recurs in the next unit, as part of ምድረ ዐውሎ ወመርቄ). ደደክ and አስሐትያ I read as names or kinds of land and cannot identify; the second may carry a feminine ending. The tone is plain: the speaker is running down Ethiopia as cold, murky and barren.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ኖሕ ፡ አመ ፡ ይትካፈሉ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ሴም ፡ ወካም ፡ ወያፌት ፡ ነጸርዋ ፡ በጥበብ ፡ ለሀገርከ ፡ ከመ ፡ ስፍሕት ፡ ወረሓብ ፡ ወምድረ ፡ ዐውሎ ፡ ወመርቄ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ወወሀብዎ ፡ ለከናኦን ፡ ወልደ ፡ ካም ፡ ክፍሎ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወለዘርኡ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ።
sentences.l: For sons-of Noah, when they-divided land, Shem and-Ham and-Japheth, they-looked-at-her in-wisdom, your-country, as wide and-ረሓብ and-land-of storm and-መርቄ it; and-they-gave-him to-Canaan son-of Ham, his-portion to-him and-to-his-seed until for-ever.
sentences.i: for when the sons of Noah, Shem and Ham and Japheth, divided the earth among themselves, they looked at your country with wisdom and saw it as wide and ረሓብ (broad, or perhaps barren?), a land of storm and መርቄ (?); and they gave Canaan, the son of Ham, his portion, to him and to his seed forever.
sentences.n: ደቂቀ ኖሕ 'sons-of Noah' (construct plural; ደቂቅ 'sons, children'). አመ ይትካፈሉ 'when they divided' (አመ + a subjunctive of ተካፈለ 'divide among themselves'); Shem, Ham and Japheth (ሴም ወካም ወያፌት) are in apposition, after the object ምድረ 'the earth' (Genesis 10; 9:25-27). ነጸርዋ 'they looked at her' (ነጸረ + -ዋ); the object is then named with ለሀገርከ 'your country' (the ለ- marks it). The adjectives ስፍሕት 'wide' and ረሓብ (either 'broad' or, from the noun ረሀብ, 'famine'; I mark it) lead into ምድረ ዐውሎ 'land of storm' (ዐውሎ). ወወሀብዎ 'and they gave him': the -ዎ is masculine, so it is Canaan, taken up again by ለከናኦን (the country is feminine and would need -ዋ, as in ነጸርዋ above). ለከናኦን ወልደ ካም: the land goes to Canaan, son of Ham; the text names Canaan here, not Cush (the Ethiopian line), and I translate what is written. ክፍሎ 'his portion' (ክፍል + -ኦ, accusative) is then what they gave: 'they gave Canaan his portion', ሎቱ 'to him' repeating the recipient. ለዘርኡ 'to his seed'; እስከ ለዓለም 'until for-ever'.

sentences.t: ወምድርሰ ፡ እንቲአነ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ርስት ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ዘወሀበነ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በከመ ፡ መሐለ ፡ ለአበዊነ ፡ ምደር ፡ እንተ ፡ ትውሕዝ ፡ ሐሊበ ፡ ወመዓረ ፡ እንተ ፡ ትከውን ፡ ሲሳየ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሐዘን ፡ እንተ ፡ ትሁብ ፡ ፍሬሃ ፡ በበ ፡ ጊዜሃ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ምንዳቤ ፤
sentences.l: And-the-land-indeed ours, land-of inheritance it, which gave-us God as swore to-our-fathers: land which flows milk and-honey, which is food without grief, which gives her-fruit in-its-seasons without affliction;
sentences.i: But our land is a land of inheritance, which God gave us, as He swore to our fathers: a land that flows with milk and honey, that is sustenance without sorrow, that yields its fruit in its seasons without affliction;
sentences.n: ወምድርሰ 'and as for the land' (-ሰ emphatic). እንቲአነ 'ours' (feminine, to agree with ምድር). ዘወሀበነ is ዘ- + ወሀበ 'gave' + -ነ 'us'; በከመ መሐለ 'as he swore' (መሐለ 'swear'); ለአበዊነ 'to our fathers' (አበው, plural of አብ). The promise is Exodus 3:8, 'a land flowing with milk and honey', retold as God's oath to the patriarchs. ምደር is a misspelling of ምድር (probably Bezold's or the digitizer's slip); I read it as 'land'. እንተ is the feminine relative ('which'), repeated before each verb: ትውሕዝ 'it flows', ትከውን 'it is/becomes', ትሁብ 'it gives'. ሐሊበ ወመዓረ 'milk and honey' (accusatives). ሲሳየ 'food, sustenance' is the predicate. ዘእንበለ ሐዘን / ምንዳቤ 'without sorrow / affliction'. በበ ጊዜሃ 'in each of its seasons' (በበ distributive; ጊዜ 'time' + -ሃ 'its').

sentences.t: እንተ ፡ ዘልፈ ፡ ይሔውጻ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምዓመት ፡ እስከ ፡ ርእሰ ፡ ዐውደ ፡ ዓመት ፤
sentences.l: which always visits-her God from-year until head-of cycle-of year;
sentences.i: which God tends continually, from year to the head of the year's cycle;
sentences.n: ዘልፈ 'always, continually'. ይሔውጻ is 3ms imperfect of ሐወጸ 'visit, look after' + -ዋ 'her' (the land): 'God visits/watches over it'. This echoes Deuteronomy 11:12, a land the Lord's eyes are on 'from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year'; I name the allusion with some confidence, as the wording is close. ርእሰ ዐውደ ዓመት 'the head of the cycle of the year' is a chain of three constructs (ርእስ + ዐውድ + ዓመት); I take it as the year's turning point. The phrase recurs in a later unit.

sentences.t: ኵላ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ለከ ፡ ወንሕነኒ ፡ ለከ ፡ ወንከውነከ ፡ ርስተ ፡ ወትነብር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ብሔርነ ፡ እስመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ዘርኡ ፡ ለዳዊት ፡ እግዚኡ ፡ ለእግዚእየ ፡ ወለከ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ መንበር ፡ እንተ ፡ እስራኤል ፨
sentences.l: All-of-it she for-you, and-we-too for-you; and-we-shall-be-for-you inheritance, and-you-will-dwell in our-country; for you seed-of David, lord-of my-lord; and-for-you she this throne of Israel.
sentences.i: All of it is yours, and we too are yours; we shall be your inheritance, and you will dwell in our country; for you are the seed of David, the lord of my lord (?); and this throne of Israel is yours."
sentences.n: ኵላ is a variant of ኵሉ 'all', here fem. to agree with the land (ይእቲ 'she is'). ለከ 'to you, yours'. ወንሕነኒ 'and we also' (ንሕነ 'we' + -ኒ). ወንከውነከ ርስተ 'and we shall be to you an inheritance' (ንከውን 1cp + -ከ). ወትነብር 'and you will dwell/sit' (ነበረ). ዘርኡ ለዳዊት 'his seed, of David' = 'David's seed' (the suffix -ሁ anticipates the owner, as above). እግዚኡ ለእግዚእየ 'lord of my lord' (also anticipatory suffix): Who is meant is uncertain (?): either David, in apposition to ለዳዊት ('David, the lord of my lord', Solomon being 'my lord' and David his father and king), or the boy himself ('you are ... the lord of my lord'). The English keeps the Geʿez's own ambiguity. መንበር እንተ እስራኤል 'throne which (is) of Israel'; the throne of David passes to him. The ፨ ends Joash's speech.

sentences.t: አውሥኡ ፡ መኳንንቲሁ ፡ ለነጋዲ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ትኄይስ ፡ ምድርነ ፡ እስመ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ነፋሰ ፡ ብሔርነ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ላህበ ፡ ወሐሩረ ፡ ወሠናይ ፡ ማየ ፡ ብሔርነ ፡ ወጥዑም ፡ ወይውሕዝ ፡ አፍላገ ፡ ወዓዲ ፡ አርእስተ ፡ አድባሪነኒ ፡ ይውሕዙ ፡ ማየ ፤
sentences.l: Answered his-nobles, of-the-merchant, and-said-to-him: better our-land, for good the-air of-our-country, which-has-not flame and-heat, and-good the-water of-our-country and-sweet, and-flows rivers, and-also heads-of our-mountains-too flow water;
sentences.i: The nobles of the merchant answered and said to him: "Our land is better, for the air of our country is good, with no flame or burning heat, and the water of our country is good and sweet, and flows as rivers, and the heads of our mountains pour out water;
sentences.n: አውሥኡ is the 3mp perfect of አውሥአ. መኳንንቲሁ ለነጋዲ 'his nobles, of the merchant' (the ለ- is genitival, as before): these are the boy's own officers, now taking up the quarrel. ወይቤልዎ 'and they said to him' (ይቤሉ + -ዎ). ትኄይስ ምድርነ 'our land is better'. ነፋሰ ብሔርነ 'the air of our country' (ነፋስ 'wind, air', in construct, accusative); ዘአልቦ 'which has not' (ዘ- + አልቦ); ላህበ 'flame', ሐሩረ 'heat'. ማየ 'water'. ወይውሕዝ አፍላገ 'and it flows (as) rivers' (አፍላግ plural of ፈለግ). ወዓዲ 'and moreover'. አርእስተ አድባሪነኒ 'heads of our mountains too' (አድባር plural of ደብር + -ነ + -ኒ); ይውሕዙ ማየ 'they pour out water'.

sentences.t: ወአኮ ፡ ከመ ፡ በሀገርክሙ ፡ ዘንከሪ ፡ ዐዘቅተ ፡ ነዋኅተ ፡ ለማይ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ዘንመውት ፡ በሐሩረ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ አላ ፡ ቀትረኒ ፡ ንንዑ ፡ አራዊተ ፡ ቶራተ ፡ ወሀየላተ ፡ ወአዕዋፈ ፡ ወእንስሳ ፡ ወክረምተኒቦ ፡ ዘይሔውጸነ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምዓመት ፡ እስከ ፡ ርእሰ ፡ ዐውደ ፡ ዓመት ፤
sentences.l: And-not as in-your-country where-we-dig wells long for-water, and-not where-we-die in-heat-of sun, but noon-too we-ንንዑ wild-beasts, wild-oxen, and-ibexes, and-birds and-livestock, and-rainy-season-too-there-is which-visits-us God from-year until head-of cycle-of year;
sentences.i: not as in your country, where one digs deep wells for water, and not where one dies in the heat of the sun, but even at noon we ንንዑ (hunt? pursue?) wild beasts, wild oxen, ibexes, birds and livestock; and we have the rainy season too, with which God tends us from year to the head of the year's cycle;
sentences.n: ዘንከሪ is ዘ- 'where, in which' + ንከሪ 'we dig' (1cp imperfect of ከረየ 'dig'): the Ethiopians speak of wells dug in the other country, as if generally ('one digs'). ዐዘቅተ ነዋኅተ 'long/deep wells' (ዐዘቅት + the accusative plural adjective). ዘንመውት 'where we die' (ንመውት 1cp imperfect of ሞተ). ፀሐይ 'sun'. ቀትረኒ 'even at noon'. ንንዑ is a puzzle: it looks like a 1cp imperfect with objects following (አራዊተ 'wild beasts', ቶራተ 'wild oxen', ሀየላተ 'ibexes', አዕዋፈ 'birds', እንስሳ 'livestock'), so I give 'hunt' on the context (?), without a parse I trust. ወክረምተኒቦ is three pieces fused, ክረምት 'rainy season' + -ኒ + ቦ 'there is'. ዘይሔውጸነ 'which visits us' (ሐወጸ + -ነ), the same verb as in the Zion-land passage; 'God tends us with it'. The Ethiopians borrow Joash's own language of divine care.

sentences.t: ወቦ ፡ በሐጋይኒ ፡ ዘይበልዑ ፡ እክለ ፡ ከይዶሙ ፡ በእግር ፡ ከመ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ወዕፀውኒ ፡ ይፈርዩ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ወሥርናየኒ ፡ ወሰገመ ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ፍረያቲነ ፡ ወእንስሳነ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ወመንክር ፤
sentences.l: And-there-is in-summer-too that-which-they-eat grain, treading with-foot like land-of Egypt; and-trees-too they-bear good, and-wheat-too and-ሰገም; and-all our-fruits and-our-livestock good and-wonderful;
sentences.i: And even in summer there is grain that they eat, treading with the foot (?) as in the land of Egypt; and our trees bear good fruit, and wheat too, and ሰገም (?); and all our fruits and our livestock are good and wonderful;
sentences.n: ወቦ 'and there is' (ቦ existential); በሐጋይኒ 'in summer too'; ዘይበልዑ እክለ 'that they eat, grain' (እክል). ከይዶሙ በእግር: ከይዶሙ I parse as the 3mp gerund of ከየደ 'tread, trample' (Dillmann), 'they treading (it) with the foot'. If so the phrase echoes Deuteronomy 11:10, Egypt where one 'waters with the foot' (irrigates by foot-worked channels), which fits the following ከመ ምድረ ግብጽ 'like the land of Egypt'; I give this with reserve (?). ዕፀው 'trees' (plural), ይፈርዩ 'they bear fruit'; ሠናየ 'good' (as an object). ሥርናይ 'wheat'. ሰገም I cannot place for certain; it follows the grain, so I take it as a kind of grain (?). ፍረያቲነ 'our fruits'; ወእንስሳነ 'and our livestock'. ሠናይ ወመንክር 'good and wonderful'.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ አሐተ ፡ ብክሙ ፡ ጥበበ ፡ እንተ ፡ ትኄይሱነ ፡ እምኔነ ፡ ወባቲ ፡ ንነግድ ፡ ኀቤክሙ ።
sentences.l: But one with-you wisdom in-which you-surpass-us than-us, and-by-it we-trade to-you.
sentences.i: But there is one thing you have, a wisdom in which you surpass us, and for it we trade with you."
sentences.n: ወባሕቱ 'but'. አሐተ is the feminine accusative of አሐዱ 'one', agreeing with ጥበበ 'wisdom'. ብክሙ 'with you' = 'you have' (በ + -ክሙ). እንተ ትኄይሱነ እምኔነ: ትኄይሱነ is the 2mp imperfect of ኀየሰ + -ነ 'us' (the plural -ሱ- shows it is not the 3fs ትኄይስ used of ምድር above): 'you surpass us', with እምኔነ 'than us' repeating the comparison; እንተ is then 'in which'. ወባቲ 'and in/by her' (ባቲ = በ + -ቲ). ንነግድ ኀቤክሙ 'we trade with you' (ነገደ 'trade'). The gracious ending: the Ethiopians admit Solomon's wisdom, the reason the Queen traded and travelled.

sentences.t: ወአውሥአ ፡ ኢዮአስ ፡ መልአከ ፡ ኀይሉ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ምንት ፡ ትኄይስ ፡ እምጥበብ ፡ እስመ ፡ ጥበብ ፡ ሣረረታ ፡ ለምድር ፡ ወአጽንዐቶ ፡ ለሰማይ ፡ ወዐጸወት ፡ ልጐታተ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢትክድና ፡ ለምድር ፤
sentences.l: And-answered Joash, messenger-of his-might, of-the-king: what is-better than-wisdom? For wisdom founded-it to-the-earth, and-strengthened-it to-the-heaven, and-shut-in the-bounds of-sea, that not-she-cover the-earth;
sentences.i: Joash, the king's messenger of might, answered: "What is better than wisdom? For wisdom founded the earth, and strengthened the heaven, and shut in the bounds (?) of the sea, so that it should not cover the earth;
sentences.n: ምንት ትኄይስ እምጥበብ 'what is better than wisdom?' The reasons recall Proverbs 3:19 and 8:22-29 (the Lord founded the earth by wisdom and set a limit to the sea). ሣረረታ is 3fs perfect of ሠረረ 'found, lay a foundation' + -ታ 'it' (the earth); ጥበብ is feminine and takes feminine verbs. ለምድር and ለሰማይ mark the objects. አጽንዐቶ 'she made firm' (አጽንዐ) + -ኦ 'it' (heaven, masculine). ዐጸወት 'she shut'. ልጐታተ is a plural form I take as 'bounds, restraints' (from ልጐት, which I believe is a bridle or bit); the sea is imagined held in. ከመ ኢትክድና 'that she not cover' (ከደነ 'cover'), the sea as subject.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ተንሥኡ ፡ ንሖር ፡ ኀበ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተነድፈት ፡ ልቡ ፡ በፍቅረ ፡ ዚአከ ፡ ወሊተሰ ፡ ፈነወኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኣምጽእከ ፡ አስተፋጢንየ ፨
sentences.l: But rise, let-us-go to my-lord, for pierced his-heart in-love-of yours; and-me-indeed he-sent-me that I-bring-you, I-hastening (?).
sentences.i: But arise, let us go to my lord, for his heart is pierced with love of you; and he sent me indeed, that I might bring you in haste (?).
sentences.n: ተንሥኡ ንሖር 'rise (pl.), let us go' (imperative, then 1cp jussive of ሖረ). ተነድፈት ልቡ 'his heart was pierced/stung' (ተነድፈ, passive of ነደፈ 'sting, strike'; the verb is feminine, since ልብ may be treated as feminine): a variation on 'his heart burned' earlier. ወሊተሰ 'and me indeed'. ፈነወኒ 'he sent me'. ከመ ኣምጽእከ 'that I bring you' (ኣምጽእ is 1cs subjunctive of the A-stem አምጽአ; Bezold prints the 1cs prefix as ኣ- (so in ch. 24, 25-26, 28), as in ኣመጽኦ below). አስተፋጢንየ: the 1cs gerund (ending -የ, like ቀቲልየ 'I having killed') of አስተፋጠነ 'make haste': 'I hastening', hence 'in haste'. I have not confirmed the form against Dillmann, so the English is marked (?). The ፨ closes the section.

sentences.t: ወተንሥአ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ወአልበሶ ፡ ለኢዮአስ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዮዳሔ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ አልባሰ ፡ ወለእሊአሁ ፡ ፶ ፡ ዕደው ፤
sentences.l: And-arose son-of queen, and-clothed Joash son-of Jehoiada good garments, and-his-people 50 men;
sentences.i: The queen's son arose, and clothed Joash son of Jehoiada in fine garments, and his men also, fifty of them;
sentences.n: ወልደ ንግሥት 'son-of queen' (construct): the boy, the queen of Sheba's son. ወአልበሶ 'and he clothed him' (አልበሰ causative of ለብሰ 'wear', + -ኦ 'him'); ለኢዮአስ marks the person clothed, and ሠናየ አልባሰ 'good garments' (አልባስ plural of ልብስ, accusative) is the thing: 'clothed him with garments'. ወለእሊአሁ 'and those of his' = his companions (እሊአሁ is the plural of the possessive ዚአሁ; ለ- marks them too). ፶ is 50 (spoken ኀምሳ, ḫaməsa). ዕደው 'men' (plural of ዕድው 'man').

sentences.t: ወተንሥኡ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሖሩ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ኀበ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ።
sentences.l: And-arose to go Jerusalem to king Solomon.
sentences.i: Then they arose to go to Jerusalem, to King Solomon.
sentences.n: ወተንሥኡ 'and they arose'; ከመ ይሖሩ 'to go' (ከመ + subjunctive of ሖረ). ኢየሩሳሌም 'Jerusalem'; ኀበ ንጉሥ ሰሎሞን 'to King Solomon'.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ አልጸቁ ፡ ቀሪበ ፡ በኀበ ፡ ምርዋጸ ፡ አፍራስ ፡ ቀደመ ፡ ኢዮአስ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዮዳሔ ፡ ወቦአ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወነገሮ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ራእዩ ፡ ወአዳም ፡ ቃሉ ፡ ወይመስል ፡ ኪያሁ ፡ ወፈድፋደ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ፍኖቱ ።
sentences.l: And-when they-drew-near close at the-course-of horses, went-ahead Joash son-of Jehoiada and-entered to king Solomon, and-told-him that fair his-appearance and-ወአዳም his-word, and-he-resembles him, and-exceedingly good in-all his-way.
sentences.i: When they drew near the horse-course, Joash son of Jehoiada went ahead and came in to King Solomon, and told him that the boy's appearance was fair, and his speech ወአዳም (pleasing?), and that he resembled him, and was exceedingly good in all his bearing.
sentences.n: ወሶበ 'and when'; አልጸቁ is 3mp perfect of አልጸቀ 'draw near'; ቀሪበ 'close, near' (accusative). በኀበ 'at, by'. ምርዋጸ አፍራስ 'course of horses' (ምርዋጽ, 'a place or act of running', in construct; አፍራስ plural of ፈረስ): a racecourse or riding ground outside the city; the exact meaning is mine, from the construct. ቀደመ 'he went before'; ወቦአ 'and he entered' (ቦአ); ወነገሮ 'and he told him'. ከመ here introduces what is told, 'that'. ሠናይ ራእዩ 'good his-appearance'. ወአዳም is not clear to me; ቃሉ 'his word' is its subject, and I guess 'pleasant' (?) from context, perhaps from አደመ 'please'. ይመስል ኪያሁ 'he resembles him' (መሰለ 'be like'). ፈድፋደ ሠናይ 'exceedingly good'.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ አይቴ ፡ ሀሎ ፡ አኮኑ ፡ ከመ ፡ ታምጽእ ፡ ኪያሁ ፡ ፍጡነ ፡ ፈነውኩከ ፤
sentences.l: And-said-to-him king: where is-he? Not-indeed that you-bring him quickly I-sent-you;
sentences.i: The king said to him: "Where is he? Did I not send you so that you would bring him quickly?"
sentences.n: አይቴ ሀሎ 'where is he?' (ሀሎ 'he is'). አኮኑ is አኮ 'not' with the question particle -ኑ: 'is it not so that...?' ከመ ታምጽእ ኪያሁ 'that you bring him' (2ms subjunctive of አምጽአ). ፈነውኩከ 'I sent you' (ፈነወ 'send', 1cs + -ከ). The unit ends at ፤ and Joash replies.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ኢዮአስ ፡ ነየ ፡ አነ ፡ ኣመጽኦ ፡ ዝየ ፡ ፍጡነ ።
sentences.l: And-said Joash: behold I I-bring-him here quickly.
sentences.i: Joash said: "Behold, I will bring him here at once."
sentences.n: ነየ 'behold'. አነ 'I' (emphasis); ኣመጽኦ 'I will bring him' (1cs of the A-stem አምጽአ, Bezold's ኣ- again; the print lacks the ም of ኣምጽኦ, which I read as a slip), + ዝየ 'here', ፍጡነ 'quickly'.

sentences.t: ወሖረ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ተንሥእ ፡ ኦሊቅየ ፡ ወነዓ ፤
sentences.l: And-went and-said: rise O-my-chief and-come;
sentences.i: He went and said: "Rise, my chief, and come."
sentences.n: ወሖረ ወይቤ 'and he went and said'. ኦሊቅየ is ኦ 'O' + ሊቅ 'chief, elder' + -የ 'my': a respectful vocative. ወነዓ 'and come!' (imperative of መጽአ, sing.). The speaker addresses the boy; the Geʿez does not name him, and I supply 'he' as Joash (the context).

sentences.t: ወእንዘ ፡ ያፈጥንዎ ፡ ሐዊረ ፡ አብጽሕዎ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አንቀጸ ፡ ንጉሥ ።
sentences.l: And-while they-hasten-him going, they-brought-him to gate-of king.
sentences.i: And as they hurried him along, they brought him to the king's gate.
sentences.n: ወእንዘ 'and while'. ያፈጥንዎ 'they hasten him' (አፈጥነ + -ዎ); ሐዊረ 'going' (verbal noun, accusative). አብጽሕዎ 'they brought him' (አብጽሐ, causative of በጽሐ 'arrive', 3mp + -ዎ). አንቀጸ ንጉሥ 'gate-of king' (construct; አንቀጽ 'gate').

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ርእይዎ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ተዓይን ፡ ሰገዱ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወይቤሉ ፡ ነዋ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወፅአ ፡ እማኅደሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-when they-saw-him all ተዓይን, they-bowed to-him and-said: behold king Solomon has-come-out from-his-dwelling;
sentences.i: When they saw him, all ተዓይን (the onlookers?) bowed to him and said: "Behold, King Solomon has come out from his dwelling!";
sentences.n: ርእይዎ 'they saw him'. ኵሉ ተዓይን: ተዓይን I cannot identify; it looks like a plural participle from a verb of looking (ዐየነ 'look' is in Dillmann), so 'the onlookers' is a guess (?). ሰገዱ ሎቱ 'they bowed to him' (ሰገደ 'bow down'). ነዋ 'behold'. ወፅአ 'he has come out' (3ms perfect, ወጽአ). እማኅደሩ 'from his dwelling' (እም + ማኅደር + -ሁ). They take the boy for Solomon, since the two look alike, as Joash had just reported.

sentences.t: ወእለሂ ፡ ውስጠ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ይወፅኡ ፡ ያነክሩ ፡ ወይገብኡ ፡ ድኅሬሆሙ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ይሬእይዎ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበሩ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ያነክሩ ፡ ይወፅኡ ፡ ወይሬእይዎ ፡ በህየኒ ፡ ወየኀጥኡ ፡ ዘይብሉ ፡ ወዘይትናገሩ ።
sentences.l: And-those, inside, when they-came-out, marvelled, and-returned behind-them, and-again saw the-king upon his-throne, and-again marvelled, they-came-out and-saw him there-too, and-erred what they-say and-what they-speak.
sentences.i: And those inside, whenever they came out, were amazed; they went back, and saw the king again on his throne, and were amazed again; they came out and saw him there as well, and they went astray in what they said and what they spoke.
sentences.n: ወእለሂ 'and those too' (እለ 'those who' + -ሂ). ውስጠ 'inside'. ሶበ ይወፅኡ 'when they come out' (ወጽአ, 3mp imperfect); ያነክሩ 'they marvel' (አንከረ). ይገብኡ ድኅሬሆሙ 'they return behind them', that is, back the way they came. ይሬእይዎ 'they see him' (the imperfect of ርእየ with a lengthened first vowel). ዲበ መንበሩ 'on his throne'. በህየኒ 'there also'. The tense is habitual; I use 'whenever' to carry it. የኀጥኡ I take as 3mp imperfect of ኀጥአ 'err, lose the way'; ዘይብሉ ወዘይትናገሩ 'what they say and what they speak'. The point: the lookalike so confused the courtiers that they went back and forth between the stranger and the real king, and could not finish a sentence.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ቦአ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ ኢዮአስ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዮዳሔ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይንግሮ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ምጽአተ ፡ ዚአሁ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘቆመ ፡ ቅድመ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ አላ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ይጸዐቁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይርአዩ ፡ ኪያሁ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-when entered again Joash son-of Jehoiada, that he-tell the-king his-coming, none who-stood before king, but all Israel were-pressing to see him.
sentences.i: And when Joash son of Jehoiada went in again to tell the king of his arrival, no one stood before the king; all Israel were pressing out to see him. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.n: ወሶበ ቦአ ካዕበ 'and when he entered again'. ከመ ይንግሮ ለንጉሥ ምጽአተ ዚአሁ 'to tell the king his coming' (ነገረ 'tell', + -ኦ 'him'; ምጽአት 'coming', accusative, + ዚአሁ 'of his', the boy's). አልቦ ዘቆመ ቅድመ ንጉሥ 'there was none who stood before the king' (the court had emptied). ኵሎሙ እስራኤል 'all of Israel'; ይጸዐቁ I take as 'were pressing, thronging' (from ጸዐቀ in my reading, and not firm) (?). ከመ ይርአዩ ኪያሁ 'to see him'. The unit ends with the row of ፨ marks, which close the chapter's text.
